# Generated by iptables-save v1.8.11 — an "anti-scan block" copied from a blog
# and tightened by hand. Half of it can never match: the kernel evaluates
# --tcp-flags as (flags & MASK) == COMP, and a flag tested in COMP but absent
# from MASK is cleared by the AND before the comparison. iptables loads every
# one of these with rc 0 (measured) and says nothing.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
# "drop SYN/FIN scans" — FIN is not in the mask: (flags & SYN) == FIN is impossible. Dead. (measured: 0 packets)
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags SYN FIN -j DROP
# "drop XMAS" with the mask narrowed to SYN,ACK — FIN, RST, PSH and URG sit outside it. Dead.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags SYN,ACK FIN,SYN,RST,PSH,ACK,URG -j DROP
# The correct shapes, left alone: comp inside the mask.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags FIN,SYN,RST,PSH,ACK,URG FIN,SYN,RST,PSH,ACK,URG -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags FIN,SYN,RST,PSH,ACK,URG NONE -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags FIN,SYN FIN,SYN -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags FIN,SYN,RST,ACK SYN -m limit --limit 25/s --limit-burst 50 -j ACCEPT
# "everything that is not a SYN/FIN" — the impossible test negated is ALWAYS true:
# this ACCEPT matches every TCP packet that reaches it (measured: 12/12) and
# the port rule below never sees one.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp ! --tcp-flags SYN FIN -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
COMMIT
